- `1` - Do not merge aggregation states from different servers for distributed query processing (query completely processed on the shard, initiator only proxy the data), can be used in case it is for certain that there are different keys on different shards.
- `2` - Same as `1` but applies `ORDER BY` and `LIMIT` (it is not possible when the query processed completely on the remote node, like for `distributed_group_by_no_merge=1`) on the initiator (can be used for queries with `ORDER BY` and/or `LIMIT`).

**Example**

```sql
SELECT *
FROM remote('127.0.0.{2,3}', system.one)
GROUP BY dummy
LIMIT 1
SETTINGS distributed_group_by_no_merge = 1
FORMAT PrettyCompactMonoBlock

┌─dummy─┐
│     0 │
│     0 │
└───────┘
```

entries.name: distributed_index_analysis
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the distributed_index_analysis_* generated group.

Index analysis will be distributed across replicas.
Beneficial for shared storage and huge amount of data in cluster.
Uses replicas from cluster_for_parallel_replicas.

- [distributed_index_analysis_for_non_shared_merge_tree](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/settings/session-settings/distributed-index-analysis#distributed_index_analysis_for_non_shared_merge_tree)

entries.name: distributed_index_analysis_for_non_shared_merge_tree
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the distributed_index_analysis_* generated group.

Enable distributed index analysis even for non SharedMergeTree (cloud only engine).

entries.name: distributed_index_analysis_only_on_coordinator
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the distributed_index_analysis_* generated group.

If enabled, distributed index analysis runs only on the coordinator.
This prevents O(N^2) spawned queries when the predicate contains subqueries (e.g., `IN (SELECT ...)`),
because each follower replica would otherwise independently trigger its own distributed index analysis,
but makes distributed index analysis less efficient if large tables are used in the subqueries.

entries.name: distributed_insert_skip_read_only_replicas
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the distributed_* generated group.

Enables skipping read-only replicas for INSERT queries into Distributed.

Possible values:

- 0 — INSERT was as usual, if it will go to read-only replica it will fail
- 1 — Initiator will skip read-only replicas before sending data to shards.

entries.name: distributed_plan_default_reader_bucket_count
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the distributed_plan_* generated group.

Default number of tasks for parallel reading in distributed query. Tasks are spread across between replicas.
Used by the rule-based distributed planner. The cost-based optimizer chooses the read fan-out by estimated cost and does not use this setting.

entries.name: distributed_plan_default_shuffle_join_bucket_count
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the distributed_plan_* generated group.

Default number of buckets for distributed shuffle-hash-join.
Used by the rule-based distributed planner. The cost-based optimizer chooses the fan-out by estimated cost and does not use this setting.

entries.name: distributed_plan_execute_locally
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the distributed_plan_* generated group.

Run all tasks of a distributed query plan locally. Useful for testing and debugging.

entries.name: distributed_plan_fallback_to_local_execution
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the distributed_plan_* generated group.

When a query plan contains a step that does not support distributed execution, log the reason and execute the query on the initiator instead of throwing an exception. Disable to get an exception instead.

Only takes effect when `make_distributed_plan` (private preview) is enabled.

entries.name: distributed_plan_force_exchange_kind
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the distributed_plan_* generated group.

Force specified kind of Exchange operators between distributed query stages.

Possible values:

- '' - do not force any kind of Exchange operators, let the optimizer choose,
 - 'Persisted' - use temporary files in object storage,
 - 'Streaming' - stream exchange data over network.

entries.name: distributed_plan_force_shuffle_aggregation
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the distributed_plan_* generated group.

Use Shuffle aggregation strategy instead of PartialAggregation + Merge in distributed query plan.
Ignored where the Shuffle strategy cannot produce a correct result, for example for `GROUPING SETS` or when the aggregation must produce results in bucket order.

entries.name: distributed_plan_max_rows_to_broadcast
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the distributed_plan_* generated group.

Maximum rows to use broadcast join instead of shuffle join in distributed query plan.
A heuristic for the rule-based distributed planner. When the cost-based optimizer is enabled, the broadcast-vs-shuffle choice is made by estimated cost and this setting has no effect.

entries.name: distributed_plan_optimize_exchanges
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the distributed_plan_* generated group.

Removes unnecessary exchanges in distributed query plan. Disable it for debugging.

entries.name: distributed_plan_prefer_replicas_over_workers
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the distributed_plan_* generated group.

Serialize the distributed query plan for execution at replicas.

entries.name: distributed_plan_read_in_order
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the distributed_plan_* generated group.

Allow the read-in-order optimization for `ORDER BY` in a distributed query plan, so a sorted read of the
table's sorting key can skip the sort and stop early instead of scanning and sorting.

Off by default: the rewrite that distributes a sort assumes the sort it wraps does not depend on its input
already being ordered, and a sort that does can be fed rows through an exchange that does not preserve
order. Only shapes where no exchange survives between the read and the sort are safe today.

entries.name: distributed_plan_workers_num
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the distributed_plan_* generated group.

How many stateless workers will be used to execute this query. Zero disables stateless-worker leasing for distributed plans.

entries.name: distributed_plan_workers_provisioning_timeout_ms
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the distributed_plan_* generated group.

Total wall-clock time, in milliseconds, a query may spend provisioning stateless workers before execution: leasing them from the discovery service and verifying they are reachable. The query blocks up to this budget for the leased workers to become ready; when it elapses the query proceeds with the workers verified so far, or fails if none became available. Zero waits only for the initial lease-and-verify pass (no retries).

entries.name: distributed_product_mode
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the distributed_* generated group.

Changes the behaviour of [distributed subqueries](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/statements/in).

ClickHouse applies this setting when the query contains the product of distributed tables, i.e. when the query for a distributed table contains a non-GLOBAL subquery for the distributed table.

Restrictions:

- Only applied for IN and JOIN subqueries.
- Only if the FROM section uses a distributed table containing more than one shard.
- If the subquery concerns a distributed table containing more than one shard.
- Not used for a table-valued [remote](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/functions/table-functions/remote) function.

Possible values:

- `deny` — Default value. Prohibits using these types of subqueries (returns the "Double-distributed in/JOIN subqueries is denied" exce

entries.name: distributed_push_down_limit
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the distributed_* generated group.

Enables or disables [LIMIT](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/settings/session-settings/other#limit) applying on each shard separately.

This will allow to avoid:
- Sending extra rows over network;
- Processing rows behind the limit on the initiator.

Starting from 21.9 version you cannot get inaccurate results anymore, since `distributed_push_down_limit` changes query execution only if at least one of the conditions met:
- [distributed_group_by_no_merge](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/settings/session-settings/distributed#distributed_group_by_no_merge) > 0.
- Query **does not have** `GROUP BY`/`DISTINCT`/`LIMIT BY`, but it has `ORDER BY`/`LIMIT`.
- Query **has** `GROUP BY`/`DISTINCT`/`LIMIT BY` with `ORDER BY`/`LIMIT` and:
    - [optimize_skip_unused_shards](https://

entries.name: distributed_replica_error_cap
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the distributed_replica_* generated group.

- Type: unsigned int
- Default value: 1000

The error count of each replica is capped at this value, preventing a single replica from accumulating too many errors.

See also:

- [load_balancing](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/settings/session-settings/load-balancing#load_balancing-round_robin)

entries.name: distributed_replica_error_half_life
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the distributed_replica_* generated group.

- Type: seconds
- Default value: 60 seconds

Controls how fast errors in distributed tables are zeroed. If a replica is unavailable for some time, accumulates 5 errors, and distributed_replica_error_half_life is set to 1 second, then the replica is considered normal 3 seconds after the last error.

See also:

- [load_balancing](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/settings/session-settings/load-balancing#load_balancing-round_robin)
- [Table engine Distributed](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/engines/table-engines/special/distributed)

entries.name: distributed_replica_max_ignored_errors
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the distributed_replica_* generated group.

- Type: unsigned int
- Default value: 0

The number of errors that will be ignored while choosing replicas (according to `load_balancing` algorithm).

See also:

- [load_balancing](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/settings/session-settings/load-balancing#load_balancing-round_robin)

entries.name: do_not_merge_across_partitions_select_final
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the Other generated group.

Improve FINAL queries by avoiding merges across different partitions.

When enabled, during SELECT FINAL queries, parts from different partitions will not be merged together. Instead, merging will only occur within each partition separately. This can significantly improve query performance when working with partitioned tables.

entries.name: dynamic_disk_allow_from_env
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the dynamic_disk_* generated group.

Allow using `from_env` substitutions in the dynamic disk configuration (i.e. in the `disk()` function arguments).
Disabled by default to prevent users from reading arbitrary environment variables when defining table storage.

entries.name: dynamic_disk_allow_from_zk
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the dynamic_disk_* generated group.

Allow using `from_zk` substitutions in the dynamic disk configuration (i.e. in the `disk()` function arguments).

entries.name: dynamic_disk_allow_include

Allow using `include` in the dynamic disk configuration (i.e. in the `disk()` function arguments).

entries.name: dynamic_throw_on_type_mismatch
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the Other generated group.

When applying a function to a [Dynamic](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/data-types/dynamic) column using the default implementation,
controls what happens for rows whose actual type is incompatible with the function:
- `true` (default) — throw an exception.
- `false` — return `NULL` for those rows instead.

entries.name: empty_result_for_aggregation_by_constant_keys_on_empty_set
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the empty_result_* generated group.

Return empty result when aggregating by constant keys on empty set.

entries.name: empty_result_for_aggregation_by_empty_set
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the empty_result_* generated group.

Return empty result when aggregating without keys on empty set.

entries.name: enable_adaptive_aggregator
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_* generated group.

Enables the adaptive `GROUP BY` algorithm: every thread aggregates into its local hash table until it reaches `adaptive_aggregator_freeze_threshold` keys (or `adaptive_aggregator_freeze_threshold_bytes` of memory), then the table freezes, so that rows of already-seen (frequent) keys keep updating it in place, while new (rare) keys are routed by their hash into per-bucket backlogs and aggregated exactly once, inside the bucket-parallel merge. Frequent keys stay in small cache-resident tables, and rare keys are stored and processed once instead of once per thread.

The external aggregation settings (`max_bytes_before_external_group_by`, `max_bytes_ratio_before_external_group_by`) are honored: past the threshold the backlogs are drained early into the shared table, and if that is not

entries.name: enable_adaptive_memory_spill_scheduler
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_* generated group.

Trigger processor to spill data into external storage adaptively. Hash joins that can spill are supported at present, both
`grace_hash` and the adaptive `hash` / `parallel_hash` path.

entries.name: enable_add_distinct_to_in_subqueries
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_* generated group.

Enable `DISTINCT` in `IN` subqueries. This is a trade-off setting: enabling it can greatly reduce the size of temporary tables transferred for distributed IN subqueries and significantly speed up data transfer between shards, by ensuring only unique values are sent.
However, enabling this setting adds extra merging effort on each node, as deduplication (DISTINCT) must be performed. Use this setting when network transfer is a bottleneck and the additional merging cost is acceptable.

entries.name: enable_alp_codec
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_* generated group.

Enables the `ALP` compression codec.

entries.name: enable_automatic_decision_for_merging_across_partitions_for_final
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_* generated group.

If set, ClickHouse will automatically enable this optimization when the partition key expression is deterministic and all columns used in the partition key expression are included in the primary key.
This automatic derivation ensures that rows with the same primary key values will always belong to the same partition, making it safe to avoid cross-partition merges.

Floating-point key columns are excluded from this derivation. The `FINAL` comparator is coarser than value
identity for `Float32`, `Float64` and `BFloat16`: `-0.0` compares equal to `0.0`, and every `NaN` bit pattern
compares equal to every other. A partition expression can tell exactly those values apart, so rows the comparator treats as
one key can land in different partitions, and skipping the cross-partition merge wo

entries.name: enable_blob_storage_log
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_blob_storage_log_* generated group.

Write information about blob storage operations to system.blob_storage_log table

entries.name: enable_blob_storage_log_for_read_operations
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_blob_storage_log_* generated group.

Write information about blob storage read operations to system.blob_storage_log table.
Requires `enable_blob_storage_log` to be enabled as well.

entries.name: enable_cascades_optimizer
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_* generated group.

Enable the Cascades cost-based optimizer for distributed query plans.
Takes effect only together with `make_distributed_plan = 1`: the setting alone does not change single-node query planning.

entries.name: enable_early_constant_folding
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_* generated group.

Enable query optimization where we analyze function and subqueries results and rewrite query if there are constants there

entries.name: enable_extended_results_for_datetime_functions
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_* generated group.

Enables or disables returning results of type `Date32` with extended range (compared to type `Date`)
or `DateTime64` with extended range (compared to type `DateTime`).

Possible values:

- `0` — Functions return `Date` or `DateTime` for all types of arguments.
- `1` — Functions return `Date32` or `DateTime64` for `Date32` or `DateTime64` arguments and `Date` or `DateTime` otherwise.

The table below shows the behavior of this setting for various date-time functions.

entries.name: enable_filesystem_cache
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_filesystem_* generated group.

Use cache for remote filesystem. This setting does not turn on/off cache for disks (must be done via disk config), but allows to bypass cache for some queries if intended

entries.name: enable_filesystem_cache_log
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_filesystem_* generated group.

Allows to record the filesystem caching log for each query

entries.name: enable_filesystem_cache_on_write_operations
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_filesystem_* generated group.

Enables or disables `write-through` cache. If set to `false`, the `write-through` cache is disabled for write operations. If set to `true`, `write-through` cache is enabled as long as `cache_on_write_operations` is turned on in the server config's cache disk configuration section.
See ["Using local cache"](/concepts/features/configuration/server-config/storing-data#using-local-cache) for more details.

Cloud default value: `1`.

entries.name: enable_filesystem_read_prefetches_log
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_filesystem_* generated group.

Log to system.filesystem prefetch_log during query. Should be used only for testing or debugging, not recommended to be turned on by default

entries.name: enable_full_text_index
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_* generated group.

**Aliases**: `allow_experimental_full_text_index`

If set to true, allow using the text index.

entries.name: enable_function_early_short_circuit
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_* generated group.

Enable early short-circuit constant folding for `and` and `or` during query analysis.
When enabled, eligible dead scalar-subquery branches are analyzed to preserve their types and validate query semantics, but they are not executed. The optimization falls back to normal analysis when scalar cardinality or runtime values are required.

entries.name: enable_funnel_functions
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_* generated group.

**Aliases**: `allow_experimental_funnel_functions`

Enable functions for funnel analysis.

entries.name: enable_global_with_statement
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_* generated group.

Propagate WITH statements to UNION queries and all subqueries

entries.name: enable_group_by_top_k_optimization
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_* generated group.

Enable TopK filtering optimization during aggregation in `GROUP BY keys ORDER BY <prefix of keys> LIMIT K` queries, and in `GROUP BY keys LIMIT K` queries without `ORDER BY` (any `K` groups are a valid result there, so a sort over all keys is synthesized).

When enabled, the aggregator maintains a bounded heap of the top `K` keys seen so far and skips inserting new rows into the hash table when their grouping key cannot make it into the final result. This avoids aggregating rows that would be discarded by the subsequent `ORDER BY ... LIMIT`, and when the heap ranks the full `GROUP BY` key it also prunes evicted groups out of the intermediate hash table, bounding its size by the `LIMIT` instead of the number of distinct keys. When the `ORDER BY` covers only a proper prefix of the `G

entries.name: enable_hash_join_row_store
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_* generated group.

Enable transforming the payload of a hash join into a row-major layout.

entries.name: enable_hdfs_pread
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_* generated group.

Enable or disables pread for HDFS files. By default, `hdfsPread` is used. If disabled, `hdfsRead` and `hdfsSeek` will be used to read hdfs files.

entries.name: enable_http_compression
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_* generated group.

Enables or disables data compression in the response to an HTTP request.

For more information, read the [HTTP interface description](/concepts/features/interfaces/http).

Possible values:

- 0 — Disabled.
- 1 — Enabled.

entries.name: enable_identifier_resolve_cache
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_* generated group.

Enable the identifier resolution cache in the query analyzer. The cache shares resolved alias nodes to prevent AST explosion when the same alias is referenced multiple times. Set to false to disable caching if incorrect results are suspected.

entries.name: enable_job_stack_trace
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_* generated group.

Output stack trace of a job creator when job results in exception. Disabled by default to avoid performance overhead.

entries.name: enable_join_fixed_hash_table_conversion
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_join_* generated group.

Enable converting the hash table to a flat array for joins when the key is a single integer with a small value range.

entries.name: enable_join_key_only_hash_tables
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_join_* generated group.

Use hash tables that store the join keys alone, without a reference to a right row, for joins whose result can never contain a value taken from a right row: `LEFT ANTI`, and `LEFT SEMI` when no right column is selected. Such a table has a smaller cell and lets the right blocks be dropped instead of stored.

entries.name: enable_join_runtime_filters
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_join_* generated group.

Filter left side by set of JOIN keys collected from the right side at runtime.

entries.name: enable_join_runtime_filters_index_analysis
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_join_* generated group.

Run a second pass index analysis (via use_skip_indexes_on_data_read) to prune granules on LHS of a join.

entries.name: enable_join_transitive_predicates
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_join_* generated group.

Infer transitive equi-join predicates from existing join conditions.
For example, given `A.x = B.x` and `B.x = C.x`, a synthetic `A.x = C.x` predicate
is added so the join order optimizer can consider direct (A JOIN C) plans.

entries.name: enable_json_ast_dialect
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_* generated group.

Enable the `clickhouse_json` value of the `dialect` setting.

When `dialect` is set to `clickhouse_json`, queries are interpreted as JSON ASTs
(the output of `parseQueryToJSON`) instead of SQL text. The `SET` query is still
parsed as plain SQL so that the dialect can be switched back.

Example:

**Example**

```sql
SET enable_json_ast_dialect = 1;
SET dialect = 'clickhouse_json';

-- Subsequent queries are parsed as JSON ASTs:

```

entries.name: enable_json_lazy_type_hints
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_* generated group.

**Aliases**: `allow_experimental_json_lazy_type_hints`

Enables lazy type hints for the [JSON](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/data-types/newjson) type.

With this setting enabled, `ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY COLUMN json JSON(path TypeName)` that only adds or changes
type hints is a metadata-only operation: the type hints are applied at query time for existing parts and
materialized during inserts and background merges instead of rewriting the historical data.

entries.name: enable_lazy_columns_replication
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_* generated group.

Enables lazy columns replication in `JOIN`, `ARRAY JOIN` and lambda captures of higher-order functions (e.g. `arrayMap`), it allows to avoid unnecessary copy of the same rows multiple times in memory.

entries.name: enable_lightweight_delete
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_lightweight_* generated group.

**Aliases**: `allow_experimental_lightweight_delete`

Enable lightweight DELETE mutations for mergetree tables.

entries.name: enable_lightweight_update
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_lightweight_* generated group.

**Aliases**: `allow_experimental_lightweight_update`

Allow to use lightweight updates.

entries.name: enable_materialized_cte
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_* generated group.

Enable materialized common table expressions (`WITH <name> AS MATERIALIZED (<subquery>)`).
When enabled, a CTE declared as `MATERIALIZED` that is referenced more than once is executed once, stored in a temporary table, and all references read from that table. A CTE referenced only once is inlined as an ordinary CTE to avoid the overhead.
When disabled, the `MATERIALIZED` keyword is ignored: the CTE is inlined at each reference like an ordinary CTE, and a warning is logged.

entries.name: enable_materialized_postgresql_table
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_* generated group.

**Aliases**: `allow_experimental_materialized_postgresql_table`

Allows to use the `MaterializedPostgreSQL` table engine.

entries.name: enable_memory_bound_merging_of_aggregation_results
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_* generated group.

Enable memory bound merging strategy for aggregation.

entries.name: enable_multiple_prewhere_read_steps
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_* generated group.

Move more conditions from WHERE to PREWHERE and do reads from disk and filtering in multiple steps if there are multiple conditions combined with AND

entries.name: enable_named_columns_in_function_tuple
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_* generated group.

Generate named tuples in function tuple() when all names are unique and can be treated as unquoted identifiers.

entries.name: enable_nullable_tuple_type
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_* generated group.

**Aliases**: `allow_experimental_nullable_tuple_type`

Allows creation of [Nullable](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/data-types/nullable) [Tuple](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/data-types/tuple) columns in tables.

This setting does not control whether extracted tuple subcolumns can be `Nullable` (for example, from Dynamic, Variant, JSON, or Tuple columns).
Use `allow_nullable_tuple_in_extracted_subcolumns` to control whether extracted tuple subcolumns can be `Nullable`.

entries.name: enable_optimize_predicate_expression
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_optimize_predicate_expression_* generated group.

Turns on predicate pushdown in `SELECT` queries.

Predicate pushdown may significantly reduce network traffic for distributed queries.

Possible values:

- 0 — Disabled.
- 1 — Enabled.

Usage

Consider the following queries:

1.  `SELECT count() FROM test_table WHERE date = '2018-10-10'`
2.  `SELECT count() FROM (SELECT * FROM test_table) WHERE date = '2018-10-10'`

If `enable_optimize_predicate_expression = 1`, then the execution time of these queries is equal because ClickHouse applies `WHERE` to the subquery when processing it.

If `enable_optimize_predicate_expression = 0`, then the execution time of the second query is much longer because the `WHERE` clause applies to all the data after the subquery finishes.

entries.name: enable_optimize_predicate_expression_to_final_subquery
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_optimize_predicate_expression_* generated group.

Allow push predicate to final subquery.

entries.name: enable_order_by_all
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_* generated group.

Enables or disables sorting with `ORDER BY ALL` syntax, see [ORDER BY](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/statements/select/order-by).

Possible values:

- 0 — Disable ORDER BY ALL.
- 1 — Enable ORDER BY ALL.

Query:

Result:

**Example**

```sql
CREATE TABLE TAB(C1 Int, C2 Int, ALL Int) ENGINE=Memory();

INSERT INTO TAB VALUES (10, 20, 30), (20, 20, 10), (30, 10, 20);

SELECT * FROM TAB ORDER BY ALL; -- returns an error that ALL is ambiguous

SELECT * FROM TAB ORDER BY ALL SETTINGS enable_order_by_all = 0;
```

entries.name: enable_packed_string_keys_in_aggregation
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_* generated group.

Use a hash table keyed by 16-byte packed string references (`PackedStringRef`) for `GROUP BY` with a single non-nullable `String` key. Keys of up to 11 bytes are stored inline in the packed reference; longer keys are referenced in an arena.
This is faster for most workloads, but can be slower than the legacy method for `GROUP BY` with very few distinct keys longer than 11 bytes (most noticeably 12..24 bytes), where the legacy hash table keeps keys inline in the cell while the packed one dereferences the arena pointer on every probe.
When disabled, the legacy `StringHashTable`-based method (the default before 26.8) is used.

All servers participating in a distributed query must agree on this value: with `distributed_aggregation_memory_efficient`, two-level bucket numbers depend on t

entries.name: enable_parallel_blocks_marshalling
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_parallel_* generated group.

Affects only distributed queries. If enabled, blocks will be (de)serialized and (de)compressed on pipeline threads (i.e. with higher parallelism that what we have by default) before/after sending to the initiator.

entries.name: enable_parallel_single_level_merge
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_parallel_* generated group.

Parallelize the final merge of the per-thread single-level aggregation hash tables. The key space is split into disjoint partitions by key hash, and each partition is merged independently: the merging thread enumerates all per-thread tables and combines the keys that belong to its partition, so no two threads ever touch the same key. If the setting is turned off, the single-level tables are merged serially on one thread. Aggregation by 8- and 16-bit keys keeps its own range-partitioned parallel merge regardless of this setting.

entries.name: enable_parsing_to_custom_serialization
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_* generated group.

If true then data can be parsed directly to columns with custom serialization (e.g. Sparse) according to hints for serialization got from the table.

entries.name: enable_positional_arguments
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_positional_arguments_* generated group.

Enables or disables supporting positional arguments for [GROUP BY](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/statements/select/group-by), [LIMIT BY](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/statements/select/limit-by), [ORDER BY](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/statements/select/order-by) statements.

Possible values:

- 0 — Positional arguments aren't supported.
- 1 — Positional arguments are supported: column numbers can use instead of column names.

Query:

Result:

**Example**

```sql
CREATE TABLE positional_arguments(one Int, two Int, three Int) ENGINE=Memory();

INSERT INTO positional_arguments VALUES (10, 20, 30), (20, 20, 10), (30, 10, 20);

SELECT * FROM positional_arguments ORDER BY 2,3;
```

entries.name: enable_positional_arguments_for_projections
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_positional_arguments_* generated group.

Enables or disables supporting positional arguments in PROJECTION definitions. See also [enable_positional_arguments](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/settings/session-settings/enable-positional-arguments#enable_positional_arguments) setting.

This is an expert-level setting, and you shouldn't change it if you're just getting started with ClickHouse.

Possible values:

- 0 — Positional arguments aren't supported.
- 1 — Positional arguments are supported: column numbers can use instead of column names.

entries.name: enable_producing_buckets_out_of_order_in_aggregation
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_* generated group.

Allow memory-efficient aggregation (see `distributed_aggregation_memory_efficient`) to produce buckets out of order.
It may improve performance when aggregation bucket sizes are skewed by letting a replica to send buckets with higher id-s to the initiator while it is still processing some heavy buckets with lower id-s.
The downside is potentially higher memory usage.

entries.name: enable_quantized_codec
entries.description:

Enables the `Quantized` compression codec.

entries.name: enable_reads_from_query_cache
entries.description:

If turned on, results of `SELECT` queries are retrieved from the [query cache](/concepts/features/performance/caches/query-cache).

Possible values:

- 0 - Disabled
- 1 - Enabled

entries.name: enable_s3_requests_logging
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_* generated group.

Enable very explicit logging of S3 requests. Makes sense for debug only.

entries.name: enable_scalar_subquery_optimization
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_* generated group.

If it is set to true, prevent scalar subqueries from (de)serializing large scalar values and possibly avoid running the same subquery more than once.

entries.name: enable_scopes_for_with_statement
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_* generated group.

If disabled, declarations in parent WITH cluases will behave the same scope as they declared in the current scope.

Note that this is a compatibility setting for the analyzer to allow running some invalid queries that old analyzer could execute.

entries.name: enable_shared_storage_snapshot_in_query
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_* generated group.

If enabled, all subqueries within a single query will share the same StorageSnapshot for each table.
This ensures a consistent view of the data across the entire query, even if the same table is accessed multiple times.

This is required for queries where internal consistency of data parts is important. Example:

Without this setting, the outer and inner queries may operate on different data snapshots, leading to incorrect results.

Possible values:

- 0 - Disabled
- 1 - Enabled

**Example**

```sql
SELECT
    count()
FROM events
WHERE (_part, _part_offset) IN (
    SELECT _part, _part_offset
    FROM events
    WHERE user_id = 42
)
```

entries.name: enable_sharing_sets_for_mutations
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_* generated group.

Allow sharing set objects build for IN subqueries between different tasks of the same mutation. This reduces memory usage and CPU consumption

entries.name: enable_software_prefetch_in_aggregation
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_software_* generated group.

Enable use of software prefetch in aggregation

entries.name: enable_software_prefetch_in_join
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_software_* generated group.

Enable use of software prefetch in hash join probe phase to hide memory access latency for large hash tables.

entries.name: enable_streaming_queries
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_* generated group.

Allow `SELECT ... FROM t STREAM [CURSOR '{...}']` continuous queries.
When off, any table expression using the `STREAM` modifier is rejected
at plan-build time. This is the umbrella gate for the streaming-queries
feature; additional capabilities may be gated by their own settings.

entries.name: enable_sz3_codec
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_* generated group.

Enables the `SZ3` compression codec.

entries.name: enable_time_series_aggregate_functions
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_* generated group.

**Aliases**: `allow_experimental_ts_to_grid_aggregate_function`, `allow_experimental_time_series_aggregate_functions`

Enables the `timeSeries*` aggregate functions for Prometheus-like time series resampling, rate, and delta calculation.

entries.name: enable_time_series_table
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_* generated group.

**Aliases**: `allow_experimental_time_series_table`

Allows creation of tables with the [TimeSeries](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/engines/table-engines/integrations/time-series) table engine. Possible values:
- 0 — the [TimeSeries](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/engines/table-engines/integrations/time-series) table engine is disabled.
- 1 — the [TimeSeries](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/engines/table-engines/integrations/time-series) table engine is enabled.

entries.name: enable_time_time64_type
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_* generated group.

**Aliases**: `allow_experimental_time_time64_type`

Allows creation of [Time](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/data-types/time) and [Time64](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/data-types/time64) data types.

entries.name: enable_trino_dialect
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_* generated group.

Enable the `trino` value of the `dialect` setting.

When `dialect` is set to `trino`, queries are written in Trino SQL: Trino-specific
syntax (`ARRAY[...]` literals, `TRY_CAST`, `UNNEST`, `ROW` types, `OFFSET` before `LIMIT`)
is translated to ClickHouse SQL, and Trino function names are mapped to their
ClickHouse equivalents. The `SET` query is still parsed as plain SQL so that the
dialect can be switched back.

The dialect also aligns the query semantics with Trino: `join_use_nulls` is turned
on, `use_variant_as_common_type` is turned off, and the query analyzer is turned on.
An explicit `SETTINGS` clause in the query still takes precedence.

entries.name: enable_unaligned_array_join
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the enable_* generated group.

Allow ARRAY JOIN with multiple arrays that have different sizes. When this settings is enabled, arrays will be resized to the longest one.

entries.name: enable_unique_key
entries.description:

**Aliases**: `allow_experimental_unique_key`

Allows creation of tables with the `UNIQUE KEY` clause on MergeTree-family engines.

entries.name: enable_url_encoding

Allows to enable/disable decoding/encoding path in uri in [URL](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/engines/table-engines/special/url) engine tables.

Disabled by default.

entries.name: enable_vertical_final
entries.description:

If enable, remove duplicated rows during FINAL by marking rows as deleted and filtering them later instead of merging rows

entries.name: enable_writes_to_query_cache

If turned on, results of `SELECT` queries are stored in the [query cache](/concepts/features/performance/caches/query-cache).

- 1 - Enabled

entries.name: enable_zxc_codec
entries.description:

Enables the `ZXC` compression codec.

entries.name: enforce_strict_identifier_format
entries.description:

If enabled, only allow identifiers containing alphanumeric characters and underscores.

entries.name: engine_file_allow_create_multiple_files
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the engine_file_* generated group.

Enables or disables creating a new file on each insert in file engine tables if the format has the suffix (`JSON`, `ORC`, `Parquet`, etc.). If enabled, on each insert a new file will be created with a name following this pattern:

`data.Parquet` -> `data.1.Parquet` -> `data.2.Parquet`, etc.

Possible values:
- 0 — `INSERT` query appends new data to the end of the file.
- 1 — `INSERT` query creates a new file.

entries.name: engine_file_empty_if_not_exists
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the engine_file_* generated group.

Allows to select data from a file engine table without file.

Possible values:
- 0 — `SELECT` throws exception.
- 1 — `SELECT` returns empty result.

entries.name: engine_file_skip_empty_files
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the engine_file_* generated group.

Enables or disables skipping empty files in [File](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/engines/table-engines/special/file) engine tables.

Possible values:
- 0 — `SELECT` throws an exception if empty file is not compatible with requested format.
- 1 — `SELECT` returns empty result for empty file.

entries.name: engine_file_truncate_on_insert
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the engine_file_* generated group.

Enables or disables truncate before insert in [File](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/engines/table-engines/special/file) engine tables.

Possible values:
- 0 — `INSERT` query appends new data to the end of the file.
- 1 — `INSERT` query replaces existing content of the file with the new data.

entries.name: engine_url_skip_empty_files
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the Other generated group.

Enables or disables skipping empty files in [URL](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/engines/table-engines/special/url) engine tables.

Possible values:
- 0 — `SELECT` throws an exception if empty file is not compatible with requested format.
- 1 — `SELECT` returns empty result for empty file.

entries.name: exact_rows_before_limit
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the Other generated group.

When enabled, ClickHouse will provide exact value for rows_before_limit_at_least statistic, but with the cost that the data before limit will have to be read completely

entries.name: except_default_mode
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the Other generated group.

Set default mode in EXCEPT query. Possible values: empty string, 'ALL', 'DISTINCT'. If empty, query without mode will throw exception.

entries.name: exclude_materialize_skip_indexes_on_insert
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the Other generated group.

Excludes specified skip indexes from being built and stored during INSERTs. The excluded skip indexes will still be built and stored [during merges](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/settings/merge-tree-settings/materialize#materialize_skip_indexes_on_merge) or by an explicit
[MATERIALIZE INDEX](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/statements/alter/skipping-index#materialize-index) query.

Has no effect if [materialize_skip_indexes_on_insert](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/settings/session-settings/materialize#materialize_skip_indexes_on_insert) is false.

Example:

**Example**

```sql
CREATE TABLE tab
(
    a UInt64,
    b UInt64,
    INDEX idx_a a TYPE minmax,
    INDEX idx_b b TYPE set(3)
)
ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple();

SET exclude_materialize_skip_indexes_on_insert='idx_a'; -- idx_a will be not be updated upon insert
--SET exclude_materialize_skip_indexes_on_insert='idx_a, idx_b'; -- neither index would be updated on insert

INSERT INTO tab SELECT number, number / 50 FROM numbers(100); -- only idx_b is updated

-- since it is a session setting it can be set on a per-query level
INSERT INTO tab SELECT number, number / 50 FROM numbers(100, 100) SETTINGS exclude_materialize_skip_indexes_on_insert='idx_b';

ALTER TABLE tab MATERIALIZE INDEX idx_a; -- this query can be used to explicitly materialize the index

SET exclude_materialize_skip_indexes_on_insert = DEFAULT; -- reset setting to default
```

entries.name: execute_exists_as_scalar_subquery
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the Other generated group.

Execute non-correlated EXISTS subqueries as scalar subqueries. As for scalar subqueries, the cache is used, and the constant folding applies to the result.

Cloud default value: `0`.

entries.name: experimental-features
entries.description:
ClickHouse has beta and experimental features. This documentation page discusses definition.

- May never become GA
- May be removed
- Can introduce breaking changes
- Functionality may change in the feature
- Need to be deliberately enabled
- The ClickHouse team **doesn't support** experimental features
- May lack important functionality and documentation
- Can't be enabled in the cloud

Please note: no additional experimental features are allowed to be enabled in ClickHouse Cloud other than those listed above as Beta.

entries.name: explain_query_plan_default
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the Other generated group.

Default format used by `EXPLAIN PLAN`.

Possible values:
- `pretty` (default since 26.7) — `actions`, `compact`, and `pretty` default to `true`, producing a compact, pretty, action-annotated plan.
- `legacy` — pre-26.7 output.

Specifying the `actions`, `compact`, or `pretty` options explicitly in the `EXPLAIN` statement (for example, `EXPLAIN actions = 0, compact = 0, pretty = 0 SELECT ...`) always overrides this setting.

`EXPLAIN PLAN` with `json = 1` or `distributed = 1` keeps the legacy (pre-26.7) defaults regardless of this setting, unless `actions`, `compact`, or `pretty` are set explicitly. The pretty output cannot represent JSON results or per-shard distributed plans, so those modes are only rendered correctly in legacy form.

entries.name: explain_syntax_single_record
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the Other generated group.

Return `EXPLAIN SYNTAX` output as a single record (with embedded newlines) instead of one record per line, so the result is a single, recoverable row (for example, `SELECT count() FROM (EXPLAIN SYNTAX ...)` returns `1`).

Specifying the `single_record` option explicitly in the `EXPLAIN SYNTAX` statement (for example, `EXPLAIN SYNTAX single_record = 0 SELECT ...`) always overrides this setting.

Set to `false` to restore the pre-26.8 one-record-per-line output, or set `compatibility` to any version older than `26.8`.

entries.name: external_storage_connect_timeout_sec

Connect timeout in seconds. Now supported only for MySQL

entries.name: external_storage_max_read_rows
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the external_storage_* generated group.

Limit maximum number of rows when table with external engine should flush history data. Now supported only for MySQL table engine, database engine, and dictionary. If equal to 0, this setting is disabled

entries.name: external_storage_rw_timeout_sec

Read/write timeout in seconds. Now supported only for MySQL

entries.name: external_table_functions_use_nulls
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the external_table_* generated group.

Defines how [mysql](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/functions/table-functions/mysql), [postgresql](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/functions/table-functions/postgresql) and [odbc](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/functions/table-functions/odbc) table functions use Nullable columns.

Possible values:

- 0 — The table function explicitly uses Nullable columns.
- 1 — The table function implicitly uses Nullable columns.

**Usage**

If the setting is set to `0`, the table function does not make Nullable columns and inserts default values instead of NULL. This is also applicable for NULL values inside arrays.

entries.name: external_table_strict_query
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the external_table_* generated group.

If it is set to true, a filter on the columns of an external table (`MySQL`, `PostgreSQL`, `SQLite`, `ODBC`, `JDBC`) that cannot be pushed down to the external database is rejected with an exception instead of being applied locally after the data is fetched.

The check covers the top-level `WHERE` predicate and each conjunct of a top-level `AND`. A `PREWHERE` on the columns of the external table is not a case for this setting: these table engines do not support `PREWHERE`, and such a query is rejected with `ILLEGAL_PREWHERE` regardless of the setting. The check runs only where a filter could be pushed down at all: when the external table is the only table of the query, on either side of an `INNER JOIN`, or on the preserving side of an outer join (the left side of a `LEFT JO

entries.name: extract_key_value_pairs_max_pairs_per_row
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the Other generated group.

**Aliases**: `extract_kvp_max_pairs_per_row`

Max number of pairs that can be produced by the `extractKeyValuePairs` function. Used as a safeguard against consuming too much memory.

entries.name: extremes
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the Other generated group.

Whether to count extreme values (the minimums and maximums in columns of a query result). Accepts 0 or 1. By default, 0 (disabled).
For more information, see the section "Extreme values".

entries.name: fallback_to_stale_replicas_for_distributed_queries
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the Other generated group.

Forces a query to an out-of-date replica if updated data is not available. See [Replication](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/engines/table-engines/mergetree-family/replication).

ClickHouse selects the most relevant from the outdated replicas of the table.

Used when performing `SELECT` from a distributed table that points to replicated tables.

By default, 1 (enabled).

entries.name: file_like_engine_default_partition_strategy
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the Other generated group.

Default partition strategy for file like engines. Applied only to `CREATE` queries with a path that has no glob or `{_partition_id}` placeholder. A path with `{_partition_id}` always uses `wildcard`. A path with another glob uses no partition strategy and ignores `PARTITION BY`. If this setting is `wildcard` but the path has no `{_partition_id}`, no partition strategy is used; table engines that can not persist this decision in their engine arguments (e.g. `HDFS`) reject such a `CREATE` instead.

entries.name: filesystem_cache_allow_background_download
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the filesystem_cache_* generated group.

Allow filesystem cache to enqueue background downloads for data read from remote storage. Disable to keep downloads in the foreground for the current query/session.

entries.name: filesystem_cache_boundary_alignment
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the filesystem_cache_* generated group.

Filesystem cache boundary alignment. For non-disk read (e.g. for cache of remote table engines / table functions) value 0 means no alignment. For disk read (e.g. for MergeTree tables on a disk with cache) value 0 means that `boundary_alignment` from the cache configuration is used.

entries.name: filesystem_cache_enable_background_download_during_fetch
entries.description:

Only has an effect in ClickHouse Cloud. Wait time to lock cache for space reservation in filesystem cache

entries.name: filesystem_cache_enable_background_download_for_metadata_files_in_packed_storage
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the filesystem_cache_* generated group.

Only has an effect in ClickHouse Cloud. Wait time to lock cache for space reservation in filesystem cache

entries.name: filesystem_cache_max_download_size
entries.description:

Max remote filesystem cache size that can be downloaded by a single query

entries.name: filesystem_cache_name
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the filesystem_cache_* generated group.

Filesystem cache name to use for stateless table engines or data lakes

entries.name: filesystem_cache_prefer_bigger_buffer_size
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the filesystem_cache_* generated group.

Prefer bigger buffer size if filesystem cache is enabled to avoid writing small file segments which deteriorate cache performance. On the other hand, enabling this setting might increase memory usage.

entries.name: filesystem_cache_reserve_space_wait_lock_timeout_milliseconds
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the filesystem_cache_* generated group.

Wait time to lock cache for space reservation in filesystem cache

entries.name: filesystem_cache_segments_batch_size
entries.description:

Limit on size of a single batch of file segments that a read buffer can request from cache. Too low value will lead to excessive requests to cache, too large may slow down eviction from cache

entries.name: filesystem_cache_skip_download_if_exceeds_per_query_cache_write_limit
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the filesystem_cache_* generated group.

**Aliases**: `skip_download_if_exceeds_query_cache`

Skip download from remote filesystem if exceeds query cache size

entries.name: filesystem_cache_verbose_logging
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the filesystem_cache_* generated group.

Emit `TEST`-level log messages for every filesystem cache buffer refill (state of the read, remaining size to read, bytes read). Only for debugging: the messages are formatted once per read, so enabling it on a query that does many small cached reads adds a large amount of logging overhead. The messages are only visible when the log level is `test` anyway (see `send_logs_level`).

entries.name: filesystem_cache_wait_for_concurrent_download_timeout_milliseconds
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the filesystem_cache_* generated group.

Maximum time to wait for a file segment which is being downloaded to the filesystem cache by a concurrent query. When the timeout is reached, the read bypasses the filesystem cache for that range and reads directly from remote storage, while the concurrent download continues to fill the cache. Value `0` means do not wait at all: bypass the cache immediately if the needed range is not downloaded yet. Lowering this value bounds the tail latency of cache-hit reads which would otherwise wait for another query's download pace at the cost of additional requests to remote storage.

entries.name: filesystem_prefetch_max_memory_usage
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the filesystem_prefetch_* generated group.

Maximum memory usage for prefetches.

Cloud default value: 10% of total memory.

entries.name: filesystem_prefetch_step_bytes
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the filesystem_prefetch_* generated group.

Prefetch step in bytes. Zero means `auto` - approximately the best prefetch step will be auto deduced, but might not be 100% the best. The actual value might be different because of setting filesystem_prefetch_min_bytes_for_single_read_task

entries.name: filesystem_prefetch_step_marks
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the filesystem_prefetch_* generated group.

Prefetch step in marks. Zero means `auto` - approximately the best prefetch step will be auto deduced, but might not be 100% the best. The actual value might be different because of setting filesystem_prefetch_min_bytes_for_single_read_task

entries.name: filesystem_prefetches_limit
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the Other generated group.

Maximum number of prefetches. Zero means unlimited. A setting `filesystem_prefetches_max_memory_usage` is more recommended if you want to limit the number of prefetches

entries.name: filter
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the Other generated group.

Adds a `WHERE` clause to the query as a wrapping subquery. Multiple filters are combined with AND. The HTTP interface allows multiple `filter` URL parameters which are combined with AND in order, and with the value of this setting.

This is a query-construction setting applied by the engine on the parsed query (wrapping it as a derived table), so it composes with the existing query and works on every protocol: it can be supplied via the HTTP URL parameter, an in-query `SETTINGS` clause, or a user profile.

It shapes result-producing `SELECT` / `UNION` queries. For a write query (`INSERT … SELECT`, `CREATE … AS SELECT`) it takes effect only when the source `SELECT` carries it in its own `SETTINGS` clause; a value inherited from a profile or session, or set on the `INSERT` / `CREATE` stat

entries.name: final
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the Other generated group.

Automatically applies [FINAL](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/statements/select/from#final-modifier) modifier to all tables in a query, to tables where [FINAL](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/statements/select/from#final-modifier) is applicable, including joined tables and tables in sub-queries, and
distributed tables.

Possible values:

- 0 - disabled
- 1 - enabled

Example:

**Example**

```sql
CREATE TABLE test
(
    key Int64,
    some String
)
ENGINE = ReplacingMergeTree
ORDER BY key;

INSERT INTO test FORMAT Values (1, 'first');
INSERT INTO test FORMAT Values (1, 'second');

SELECT * FROM test;
┌─key─┬─some───┐
│   1 │ second │
└─────┴────────┘
┌─key─┬─some──┐
│   1 │ first │
└─────┴───────┘

SELECT * FROM test SETTINGS final = 1;
┌─key─┬─some───┐
│   1 │ second │
└─────┴────────┘

SET final = 1;
SELECT * FROM test;
┌─key─┬─some───┐
│   1 │ second │
└─────┴────────┘
```

entries.name: finalize_projection_parts_synchronously
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the Other generated group.

When enabled, projection parts are finalized synchronously during INSERT, reducing peak memory usage at the cost of reduced S3 upload parallelism. By default, each projection's output stream is kept alive until the entire part (including all projections) is finalized, which allows overlapping S3 uploads but increases peak memory proportional to the number of projections. This setting only affects the INSERT path; merge and mutation already finalize projections synchronously.

entries.name: flatten_nested
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the Other generated group.

Sets the data format of a [nested](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/data-types/nested-data-structures/index) columns.

Possible values:

- 1 — Nested column is flattened to separate arrays.
- 0 — Nested column stays a single array of tuples.

**Usage**

If the setting is set to `0`, it is possible to use an arbitrary level of nesting.

Query:

Result:

Query:

Result:

**Example**

```sql
SET flatten_nested = 1;

SHOW CREATE TABLE t_nest;
```

ClickHouse session settings in the force_* generated group.

Disables query execution if the index can't be used by date.

If `force_index_by_date=1`, ClickHouse checks whether the query has a date key condition that can be used for restricting data ranges. If there is no suitable condition, it throws an exception. However, it does not check whether the condition reduces the amount of data to read. When enabled, a projection that can serve the query is used even if it requires reading more marks than the table itself, and the query fails with the `PROJECTION_NOT_USED` error when no projection can be used.

Possible values:

- 1 — Projection optimization is obligatory.

- 1 — Enabled. Query execution is disabled only if the table has a sharding key.

entries.name: framing_output_format
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the Other generated group.

Allows to multiplex different parts of the query response in a single stream: chunks of data, totals and extremes, progress packets, profile events (metrics), and server logs - everything that the native protocol supports.

Framing formats are independent of output formats: they encapsulate bytes produced by any output format, by separating and potentially encoding these chunks of bytes. The concatenation of the payloads of all `data`, `totals` and `extremes` packets is exactly what the output format would have produced without framing. Auxiliary packets (progress, logs, profile events, exceptions) are represented as JSON.

One deliberate exception: an output format that drops totals and extremes in its plain output because it cannot represent them (the `JSONCompactEachRow` family) does

entries.name: fsync_metadata

entries.name: function_base58_max_input_size
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the function_* generated group.

Maximum size, in bytes, of a single input value for the functions `base58Encode`, `base58Decode` and `tryBase58Decode`. The generic `base58` conversion is quadratic in the input length, so a single large value can run for a very long time. `base58` is meant for short data (keys, hashes, addresses), so the default of 10 KB is a generous safety threshold. `base58Encode` and `base58Decode` throw `TOO_LARGE_STRING_SIZE` for larger inputs, while `tryBase58Decode` returns an empty string. A value of `0` disables the limit (the behavior before this setting was introduced). The linear `base32` and `base64` functions are unaffected.

entries.name: group_by_top_k_optimization_observation_rows

The effective window is at least twice the heap's reserved size, so a heap always gets a chance to fill before being judged. `0` disables this freeze (the heap still freezes when a boundary tie-set overgrows it).

This has no effect on `GROUP BY keys LIMIT K` queries without `ORDER BY`, where the freeze is always disabled: that shape's plan contains a synthesized sort that only pays off while the heap bounds the hash table, so freezing the heap would leave a plan slower than the un-optimized one

- 1 — ClickHouse executes `GROUP BY` the same way as the SQL standard says. The types of aggregation keys are converted to [Nullable](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/data-types/nullable). Columns for corresponding aggregation keys are filled with [NULL](https://clickhouse.com/docs/re

entries.name: http_allow_database_as_path
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the http_* generated group.

If enabled, the HTTP interface recognizes a `/database/` component in the URL path and uses it as the current database.

This is a per-user setting that controls whether a routed path-style request is interpreted. Routing itself is gated globally by the server-level `http_allow_path_requests` configuration setting (off by default), which must be enabled for the HTTP interface to route a path-style request (such as `/my_db/my_table.csv`) to the query handler at all — that routing decision is made before the request is authenticated, so it cannot depend on a per-user setting. When `http_allow_path_requests` is off, unknown paths return a plain `404`. After routing, this setting is re-checked against the authenticated user's effective settings, so it can be enabled selectively per user,

entries.name: http_allow_filters_as_path
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the http_* generated group.

If enabled, the HTTP interface recognizes `/name=value/` components in the path (hive partitioning style) and translates them to filters combined with AND. Operators `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=`, `!=`, `<>` are also recognized.

Like [`http_allow_database_as_path`](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/settings/session-settings/http#http_allow_database_as_path), this is a per-user setting; routing of path-style requests is gated globally by the server-level `http_allow_path_requests` configuration setting (routing happens before authentication).

entries.name: http_allow_filters_as_unrecognized_url_parameters
entries.description:

If enabled, any URL parameter not recognized as a known parameter, setting, or `param_*` prefix is treated as a filter and combined with AND. Two forms are accepted:

- A plain `name=value` becomes the equality `` `name` = 'value' `` (the identifier is back-quoted, the value is quoted as a string literal).
- A comparison operator (`!=`, `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=`, `<>`) makes it a comparison: either split across the parameter (`?a!=2`, `?a>=2`) or written inline when the URL has no `=` to split on (`?a<>2`, `?f(x)>3`), in which case the reassembled `name[=value]` is parsed as a full SQL expression.

entries.name: http_allow_table_as_file

If enabled, the HTTP interface recognizes the last URL path component as a table name in the form `table`, `table.format`, or `table.format.compression`. The path is interpreted as `SELECT * FROM table`.

Like [`http_allow_database_as_path`](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/settings/session-settings/http#http_allow_database_as_path), this is a per-user setting; routing of path-style requests is gated globally by the server-level `http_allow_path_requests` configuration setting (routing happens before authentication).

entries.name: iceberg_manifest_decode_concurrency
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the iceberg_* generated group.

**Aliases**: `iceberg_delete_manifest_decode_concurrency`

Maximum number of Iceberg manifest files decoded concurrently while reading a table.

Delete manifests are all decoded before any data file is read; data manifests are decoded while the list of data files for the query is produced, and new ones are decoded only as the query consumes already decoded entries. Decoding several manifests at a time overlaps the object storage round-trips and the per-entry pruning work.

Higher values raise peak memory when the Iceberg metadata files cache is disabled or full, since each in-flight manifest then holds its own decoded contents.

Must be greater than zero; `1` decodes the manifests one at a time.

Ignoring the `xy_idx` index:

**Example**

```sql
CREATE TABLE data
(
    key Int,
    x Int,
    y Int,
    INDEX x_idx x TYPE minmax GRANULARITY 1,
    INDEX y_idx y TYPE minmax GRANULARITY 1,

```

- 1 — Enabled.

For the replicated tables by default the only 100 of the most recent blocks for each partition are deduplicated (see [replicated_deduplication_window](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/settings/merge-tree-settings/replicated-deduplication-window#repli

entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the insert_* generated group.

The setting allows a user to provide own deduplication semantic in MergeTree/ReplicatedMergeTree
For example, by providing a unique value for the setting in each INSERT statement,
user can avoid the same inserted data being deduplicated.

Possible values:

- Any string

`insert_deduplication_token` is used for deduplication _only_ when not empty.

For the replicated tables by default the only 100 of the most recent inserts for each partition are deduplicated (see [replicated_deduplication_window](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/settings/merge-tree-settings/replicated-deduplication-window#replicated_deduplication_window), [replicated_deduplication_window_seconds](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/settings/merge-tree-settings/replicated-deduplication-window#replicated_deduplicati

**Example**

```sql
CREATE TABLE test_table
( A Int64 )
ENGINE = MergeTree
ORDER BY A
SETTINGS non_replicated_deduplication_window = 100;

INSERT INTO test_table SETTINGS insert_deduplication_token = 'test' VALUES (1);

-- the next insert won't be deduplicated because insert_deduplication_token is different
INSERT INTO test_table SETTINGS insert_deduplication_token = 'test1' VALUES (1);

-- the next insert will be deduplicated because insert_deduplication_token
-- is the same as one of the previous
INSERT INTO test_table SETTINGS insert_deduplication_token = 'test' VALUES (2);

SELECT * FROM test_table

┌─A─┐
│ 1 │
└───┘
┌─A─┐
│ 1 │
└───┘
```

Whether a hash-based algorithm spills to disk is not part of this choice: [`max_bytes_before_external_join`](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/settings/session-settings/max-bytes#max_bytes_before_external_join) / [`max_bytes_ratio_before_external_join`](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/settings/session-settings/max-bytes#max_bytes_ratio_before_external_join) are the spill threshold for all of them (and once one of the two is non-zero, `enable_adaptive_memory_spill_scheduler` can spill the join earlier still, under memory pressure), and

entries.name: join_any_take_last_row
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the join_* generated group.

Changes the behaviour of join operations with `ANY` strictness when the right table has more than one matching row for a key.

This setting applies to [`Join`](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/engines/table-engines/special/join) engine tables and hash-based join algorithms.

If a join is built in parallel, the order of rows can be non-deterministic. This means that `join_any_take_last_row = 1` can return a non-deterministic row for `ANY JOIN` queries.

Possible values:

- 0 — If the right table has more than one matching row, only the first one found is joined.
- 1 — If the right table has more than one matching row, only the last one found is joined.

See also:

- [JOIN clause](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/statements/select/join)
- [Join table engine](https://clickhouse.com/docs

entries.name: join_default_strictness
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the join_* generated group.

Sets default strictness for [JOIN clauses](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/statements/select/join).

Possible values:

- `ALL` — If the right table has several matching rows, ClickHouse creates a [Cartesian product](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cartesian_product) from matching rows. This is the normal `JOIN` behaviour from standard SQL.
- `ANY` — If the right table has several matching rows, only the first one found is joined. If the right table has only one matching row, the results of `ANY` and `ALL` are the same.
- `ASOF` — For joining sequences with an uncertain match.
- `Empty string` — If `ALL` or `ANY` is not specified in the query, ClickHouse throws an exception.

entries.name: join_on_disk_max_files_to_merge
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the join_* generated group.

Limits the number of files allowed for parallel sorting in MergeJoin operations when they are executed on disk.

The bigger the value of the setting, the more RAM is used and the less disk I/O is needed.

Possible values:

- Any positive integer, starting from 2.

entries.name: join_output_by_rowlist_perkey_rows_threshold
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the join_* generated group.

The lower limit of per-key average rows in the right table to determine whether to output by row list in hash join.

entries.name: join_overflow_mode
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the join_* generated group.

Defines what action ClickHouse performs when a join reaches any of the following limits:

- [max_bytes_in_join](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/settings/session-settings/max-bytes#max_bytes_in_join)
- [max_rows_in_join](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/settings/session-settings/max-rows#max_rows_in_join)

Every hash-based [`join_algorithm`](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/settings/session-settings/join#join_algorithm)
value honors this setting, including the ones that spill to disk: reaching the
limit stops the query rather than triggering a spill. The exception is
`legacy_join_size_limits_trigger_spilling`: with it on, the part of a join that
already runs on disk spills further instead of acting on this setting.
`ie_join` honors it as well, on the input it accumulates

entries.name: join_runtime_bloom_filter_bytes
entries.description:

Size in bytes of a bloom filter used as JOIN runtime filter (see enable_join_runtime_filters setting).

entries.name: join_runtime_bloom_filter_hash_functions
entries.description:

entries.name: join_runtime_filter_blocks_to_skip_before_reenabling

entries.name: join_runtime_filter_from_fixed_hash_table

entries.name: join_runtime_filter_min_probe_rows
entries.description:

If, at query planning time, the probe side of a JOIN is estimated to produce no more than this number of rows, the JOIN runtime filter is not created. Building and applying a runtime filter for a tiny probe side costs more than it saves. Set to 0 to always create the runtime filter regardless of the estimated probe size.

entries.name: join_runtime_filter_pass_ratio_threshold_for_disabling
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the join_runtime_* generated group.

If ratio of passed rows to checked rows is greater than this threshold the runtime filter is considered as poorly performing and is disabled for the next `join_runtime_filter_blocks_to_skip_before_reenabling` blocks to reduce the overhead.

entries.name: join_runtime_filter_size_from_hash_table_stats
entries.description:

entries.name: join_to_sort_maximum_table_rows

entries.name: join_use_nulls
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the join_* generated group.

Sets the type of [JOIN](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/statements/select/join) behaviour. When merging tables, empty cells may appear. ClickHouse fills them differently based on this setting.

Possible values:

- 1 — `JOIN` behaves the same way as in standard SQL. The type of the corresponding field is converted to [Nullable](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/data-types/nullable), and empty cells are filled with [NULL](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/syntax).

entries.name: joined_block_split_single_row
entries.description:

Allow to chunk hash join result by rows corresponding to single row from left table.
This may reduce memory usage in case of row with many matches in right table, but may increase CPU usage.
Note that `max_joined_block_size_rows != 0` is mandatory for this setting to have effect.
The `max_joined_block_size_bytes` combined with this setting is helpful to avoid excessive memory usage in case of skewed data with some large rows having many matches in right table.

entries.name: joined_subquery_requires_alias

entries.name: kafka_disable_num_consumers_limit

entries.name: legacy_join_size_limits_trigger_spilling
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the Other generated group.

Restores how `max_rows_in_join` and `max_bytes_in_join` worked before the spill threshold became the trigger, for
the part of a join that runs on disk: reaching one of them makes the join spill further instead of stopping the query.
`join_algorithm = 'grace_hash'` then spills on those two alone and ignores `max_bytes_before_external_join` entirely, zero
included. `hash` / `parallel_hash` still go to disk on the spill threshold and spill on either one afterwards; their
in-memory phase keeps treating the two as a hard cap, as it did before.

For queries written against the earlier meaning of these two settings; `compatibility` enables it automatically.

A server that predates this setting applies the old meaning, and cannot be told otherwise, so with
`serialize_query_plan = 1` a join whos

entries.name: lightweight_delete_mode
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the lightweight_* generated group.

A mode of internal update query that is executed as a part of lightweight delete.

Possible values:
- `alter_update` - run `ALTER UPDATE` query that creates a heavyweight mutation.
- `lightweight_update` - run lightweight update if possible, run `ALTER UPDATE` otherwise.
- `lightweight_update_force` - run lightweight update if possible, throw otherwise.

entries.name: lightweight_deletes_sync
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the lightweight_* generated group.

The same as [`mutations_sync`](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/settings/session-settings/mutations#mutations_sync), but controls only execution of lightweight deletes.

Possible values:

- [Mutations](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/statements/alter/index#mutations)

Cloud default value: `1`.

entries.name: limit
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the Other generated group.

Sets the maximum number of rows to get from the query result. It adjusts the value set by the [LIMIT](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/statements/select/limit) clause. The value is passed through to `LIMIT` and accepts everything that `LIMIT` accepts, including negative values (count from the end of the result) and fractions in `(0, 1)` (interpreted as a share of the result).

Possible values:

- 0 — The number of rows is not limited.
- Positive integer — exact number of rows.
- Negative integer — return the last N rows.
- A real number in the open range `(0, 1)` — return that fraction of the result.

This setting shapes result-producing `SELECT` / `UNION` queries. For a write query (`INSERT … SELECT`, `CREATE … AS SELECT`) it takes effect only when the source `SELECT` carries it in

entries.name: load_balancing
entries.description:
ClickHouse session settings in the load_balancing_* generated group.

Specifies the algorithm of replicas selection that is used for distributed query processing.

ClickHouse supports the following algorithms of choosing replicas:

- [Random](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/settings/session-settings/load-balancing#load_balancing-random) (by default)
- [Nearest hostname](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/settings/session-settings/load-balancing#load_balancing-nearest_hostname)
- [Hostname levenshtein distance](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/settings/session-settings/load-balancing#load_balancing-hostname_levenshtein_distance)
- [Hostname longest common prefix](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/settings/session-settings/load-balancing#load_balancing-hostname_longest_common_prefix)
- [Hostname longest common suffix](https://cl

**Example**

```sql
load_balancing = random
```

entries.name: load_balancing_first_offset
